name: Kern River High Desert Lateral

values.RouteType: Not mapped (but could be — route or endpoints are known)
values.RouteNotes: Endpoints known from the FERC notice; no public route found yet.

researcher_notes: Kern River's High Desert Lateral: FERC docket CP01-405. The July 2001 notice of application in the Federal Register describes about 31.6 miles of 24-inch lateral in San Bernardino County, California, from the Kern River and Mojave common facilities near Kramer Junction to the High Desert power plant near Victorville, with 282,000 Dth per day of design capacity. The EIA pipeline projects table for August 2026, sheet Historical Projects, Excel row 250, lists it as completed, in service September 2002, 32 miles, 24 inch, 275 MMcf per day, cost 29 million dollars. Not an existing row: Kern River's main line (P0207) runs Opal to Daggett and its Delta Lateral (P3856) is in Utah and Nevada. No existing row names Victorville or High Desert. Length of 31.6 miles is about 51 km, above the 25 km threshold. The line is operating, so the concrete step is met. Two independent origins (FERC notice and EIA table, which cites the same docket). The cost is only in the EIA table. The start location is stated as the Kern River and Mojave common facilities near Kramer Junction; the exact tie-in point was not confirmed. No route was found. A public GIS route was not searched beyond this. Route type: not mapped but could be, since the endpoints are known.
